fair_value.method: Blend of 60% forward P/E (Sept-2027 NTM adj. EPS ~$10.54 x 25x = ~$263) and 40% DCF valued at Sept 2027 (WACC 10%, terminal growth 4%, op margin rising to 27% by 2030 per the investor-day ambition, ~$250/share). Blended ~$258 for Vertiv Holdings Co (NYSE: VRT).

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM adj. EPS at Sept 2027 = 0.25 x FY27 $9.16 + 0.75 x FY28 $11.00 = $10.54; x 25x forward P/E

inputs_detail.derivation: +20% on the $9.16 FY27 consensus. Management's May 2026 framework is 20-22% revenue CAGR (2025-30) with adj. op margin going from ~23.8% (FY26 guide) to 27%+ by 2030, which implies ~22-25% EPS growth; haircut to 20% because consensus FY27 revenue ($18.2B) already runs ahead of that CAGR path, and for Q2's execution slippage.

Stock now at ~26.6x FY27 consensus ($244/$9.16). Near the 52-week high ($380) it traded at ~41-43x the FY27 EPS estimates of the time (~$8.8 60-90 days ago). With growth slowing from ~60% EPS growth (FY26) to ~20% (FY28), I apply a slight discount to today's multiple rather than a re-rating either way.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Revenue FY27 $18.2B, then +18%/15%/12%/10%/9%/8%/7%/6% to 2035 ($40.7B); adj. op margin 25% (27) -> 26% (28) -> 26.5% (29) -> 27% (2030+); tax 21%; FCF = 90% of NOPAT; WACC 10%; terminal growth 4%; valued at Sept 2027; +$2.5B net cash; 395M diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Starts slightly below management's 20-22% 5-year revenue CAGR target and data-center TAM growth of 18-20%, then fades toward nominal GDP-plus as the AI build-out matures.
FY26 guide is 23.3-24.3% and Q2 came in at 22.6%. The 2030 target is 27%+ (raised from 25%+). I assume the target is reached with no further upside.

Management targets 95-100% FCF conversion and 3-4% capex/sales, but the 10-Q shows inventories up $1.05B in 1H26 ($1.46B to $2.52B) that was funded by a $1.82B deferred-revenue build. I haircut conversion because that customer-prepayment tailwind should reverse as growth slows.

The balance sheet is near net-cash (cash $2.81B + ST inv. $0.30B vs debt $2.94B at 6/30/26), so WACC is roughly cost of equity. High beta and 60%+ realized vol argue for ~10%. Terminal growth of 4% reflects secular data-center demand.
Small allowance for SBC dilution. $2.4B of the $3.0B buyback authorization remains unused through 12/2027.
~$0.17B net cash at 6/30/26 + ~$2.5B+ annual adj. FCF, less dividends, bolt-on M&A (5 deals since Aug 2025, ~$1.5B) and up to ~$0.25B in PurgeRite/other earnouts.

bear.story: AI capex digestion: hyperscalers' FCF turns negative (Alphabet already FCF-negative in Q2 2026) and projects get pushed out. The Texas permit freeze spreads. Vertiv's multiphase project coordination problems recur, H2 2026 misses the 40%+ growth guide, and deferred revenue unwinds. FY28 EPS falls to ~$8.5 and the multiple compresses to ~16-17x, near the 52-week low.

base.story: Q3 and Q4 2026 roughly meet the $3.75B / ~40% Q3 guide, and FY26 lands at ~$6.70 EPS. 2027 guidance comes in around consensus (~$18B revenue, ~$9.2 EPS). The 800V DC sidecar ramp starts in H2 2027. The stock trades at ~25x NTM EPS of ~$10.5.

bull.story: Execution issues clear. Infrastructure-solutions (OneCore/SmartRun) orders keep ramping, 2027 guidance beats (EPS $10+), and margins reach 26%+ early. 800V and liquid-cooling content per MW expands, and the multiple re-rates to ~32x FY28 EPS of ~$13, above the prior $380 high.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$165 the stock would trade at ~18x FY27 consensus and ~15x my FY28 estimate. That level only makes sense if the market believes orders/backlog are shrinking, i.e. hyperscaler capex cuts or share loss in liquid cooling/power, rather than a timing slip. It sits well below the post-Q2 trading range and implies FY27 EPS closer to the $8.28 low estimate with de-rating. Confirming evidence would be deferred revenue falling from the $3.63B peak, FY27 guidance below ~$8.5 EPS, or a margin guide cut.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results; guide was $3.65-3.85B sales, 34-36% organic, adj. EPS $1.77-1.83, 24-25% margin. Test of whether the Q2 timing slip was recovered.
Q4 2026 results and first FY2027 guidance vs ~$18.2B revenue / $9.16 EPS consensus.
Hyperscaler Q3/Q4 capex commentary and 2027 capex budgets (Alphabet/Microsoft/Amazon/Meta)
Texas data-center permit freeze pending ERCOT/Water Development Board audits; risk of copycat state actions
Q1 and Q2 2027 results: margin progression toward 25%+ and the capacity ramp (five Americas plant expansions, Johor, Malaysia)
Initial 800V DC sidecar deployments (acceleration H2 2027); native 800V systems commercial late 2027
IEEPA tariff refund claims (CAPE process); amount and timing uncertain

key_uncertainties: Durability of hyperscaler/AI data-center capex in 2027-28 given negative hyperscaler FCF and rising debt funding
Whether the Q2 2026 multiphase-project coordination problems (internal factories feeding each other) are fixed or recur in H2 2026

Order trend: Vertiv stopped giving explicit orders/backlog figures in 2026 releases after reporting a $15.0B backlog and a ~2.9x book-to-bill in Q4 2025. Deferred revenue ($3.63B) is the only hard proxy.
Working-capital reversal: the inventory build (+$1.05B in 1H26) was offset by customer deposits, and that could swing negative
Multiple regime: the stock traded ~40x+ at the high vs ~26x now. Sentiment-driven swings (e.g., the -8% day on 2026-06-23 from Korean leveraged-ETF news) dominate the 12-month distribution.
800V DC adoption timing and competitive intensity in liquid cooling and power
reasoning: Primary documents show fundamentals still accelerating. Q2 2026 sales were $3.27B (+24%, +18% organic) and adj. EPS was $1.52 (+60%). FY26 guidance was raised a third time to $14.0B sales / $6.70 adj. EPS / $2.4-2.6B FCF, and Q3 is guided at ~40% growth. Q4 2025 backlog was $15.0B with a 2.9x book-to-bill. The May 2026 investor conference set a 20-22% revenue CAGR and 27%+ margin by 2030. The 10-Q shows the balance sheet now at net cash, deferred revenue doubled to $3.63B, inventories +$1.05B, and $2.4B of buyback authorization unused. At the Goldman conference in September, management said demand is 'strengthening' and called Q2's issue coordination rather than supply. Against this, the stock is -36% from its $380 high because of sector-wide AI-capex doubts (hyperscaler FCF strain, Texas permit freeze), the Q2 revenue-timing miss and heavy insider selling. Consensus FY27 EPS has actually risen ($8.80 to $9.16 over 90 days), so the drawdown is multiple compression to ~26.6x FY27. My fair value is ~$258: 25x a Sept-2027 NTM EPS of ~$10.5 blended with a ~$250 DCF. That is only slightly above spot because I don't assume the multiple re-expands. Given 66% realized vol, a bimodal AI-cycle outcome and a 12-month horizon, I centered a lognormal-like distribution at a ~$258 median with ~0.55 log-sigma. I fattened the far-left tail a bit for an AI-capex bust and trimmed the far right. Scenarios (bear $140/25%, base $265/50%, bull $415/25%) give a mean of ~$271, consistent with a median near $255-260 and right skew. P(>= spot $244) is ~0.54. Research was mostly primary (8-K releases, 10-Q, call transcript, investor-conference materials); I could not parse the investor-day PDF directly and used a recap for its targets. No option data was used.
